findings.finding: Powdered oral creatine monohydrate versus maltodextrin placebo is preserved, with source weight bands 2.5/5/7.5/10 g daily, nominal approximately 100 mg/kg/day up to 10 g, two 12-week periods and planned six-week washout. Shared 5 g Splenda and 250 mL skimmed milk are reported exposures, not a clinical regimen. No unsupported supplier, purity, lot, salt substitution or retail equivalence is assigned.

13 randomized (7 creatine-first/6 placebo-first), 11 completed both periods, and flowchart 13 analyzed are distinct. Native MFM rows have 12 treatment changes, 12 placebo changes and 11 paired rows; 13 complete pairs are not implied. Pandemic withdrawals, injury during washout and remote assessment are source-specific limits. The 12/1 versus 11/2 ambulant/wheelchair discrepancy remains unresolved. Secondary denominators must not be assumed equal.

Primary MFM difference +0.19 points (95% CI -0.71 to 1.08; supplementary P=.68) supplies no demonstrated motor-function benefit, not proof of zero effect. The +27.74 m walking estimate (95% CI -1.41 to 56.88; P=.06), FSHD-COM -2.06 (-4.82 to 0.71; P=.15), and timed walk/run -0.21 s (-0.45 to 0.02; P=.07) remain favorable but uncertain. PUL and each MRI interval cross zero. Scale direction and primary/secondary hierarchy are correctly separated; MRI is not functional output. Other Table 2 measures do not establish that every secondary estimate favored creatine.

source_locators: SAP Main Analysis, Definition of analysis populations, Handling of Missing Data, and secondary outcome sections
findings.finding: Treatment/period fixed effects with a participant random effect are the described primary analysis. No period effect and no treatment-period interaction are assumptions, not proven tests. The supplement says t-test p-value; some ordinal secondary SAP sections specify Wilcoxon signed-rank analysis, so one verified analytic provenance cannot be assigned to all endpoints. Qualification appropriately leaves provenance incomplete and avoids reconstructing adjusted contrasts by subtracting unadjusted means. No model was rerun.

source_locators: SAP Adjustment for Multiplicity; Subgroup Analyses
findings.finding: The retained SAP date follows the main-reported May 2021 last visit and current July 2022 completion date. Its blinded-development statement is retained without independently established unblinding timing. Friedreich-ataxia contents/abbreviations, unrelated administrative NCT03933163 and pill-count wording are real internal remnants, not proof of invalid results or misconduct. The SAP states no multiplicity adjustment and no subgroup analysis. No confirmed subgroup benefit or pediatric FSHD walking threshold is inferred.

source_locators: SAP Study Synopsis and Study Schedule
findings.finding: Current first posting 2016-10-28 precedes recruitment, but historical field versions are unread. Current enrollment 11 versus publication randomized 13 remains explicit. Listed quantitative strength, ultrasound, GPX3 and step-count outcomes have no result identified in the retained publication/supplements. Their status is unreported/unknown, not null. Current hasResults=false is a registry fact, not proof no data or other versions exist.

source_locators: primary.xml phar70025-sec-0026 Safety analysis and Discussion
supplement PDF p3 full safety table and bottom summary
findings.finding: Creatinine +12.63 micromol/L (95% CI 1.14 to 24.12; P=.031) and calculated eGFR -25.79 mL/min/1.73 m2 (-44.3 to -7.25; P=.006) are preserved exactly. The authors attribute change to creatinine production and report reversal, but creatinine-derived eGFR with no measured-GFR/cystatin-C confirmation establishes neither kidney injury nor unaffected filtration. Two missing creatine blood tests, renal exclusions, small sample and short exposure limit transfer. No AE discontinuation or creatine-related SAE is reported; the washout fall is not attributed causally to creatine.

source_locators: qualification.md What constrains confidence; Safety and competitiveness; Source and reading depth
findings.finding: The root summary is more calibrated than the paper’s general safe/well-tolerated wording and does not erase favorable uncertain estimates or earlier DMD positives. This FSHD contrast adds a controlled primary null to a mixed evidence base; it supplies no head-to-head superiority, generic no-effect conclusion, BUBR1 restoration, chromosome-fidelity or MVA endpoint. The shared exposure/function/renewal/fidelity bar and restoration-specific BUBR1 mediation distinction are appropriate.

source_locators: primary.xml phar70025-sec-0030 Conflict of interest statement
nonblocking_observations.detail: The trial reports a competitive FSHD Global Research Foundation grant and named investigators’ other pharmaceutical honoraria/grants/trial roles. These are not manufacturer sponsorship of the trial preparation or evidence that disclosures caused the findings. Root read these sections; their absence from the concise narrative does not alter its bounded conclusion.

Main Table 2 also contains FSHD-CS/CSS, ACTIVLIM, Health Index, global change and PedsQL rows; the supplementary efficacy table does not print PedsQL P values. The parent PedsQL interval is rounded to -5 to 0. Do not infer a significant effect or classify all secondary directions as favorable from this rounded endpoint. The root qualification makes neither claim.
